title: Building Mobile Features That Stay Maintainable
summary: A practical approach to balancing product speed, clear boundaries, and testable code across iOS and Flutter projects.

content.text: A mobile feature is successful when it solves the user's problem today without making tomorrow's change unnecessarily expensive. That balance starts before the first view or widget is built.
Start with a clear feature boundary
Define what the feature owns: its state, business rules, external dependencies, and navigation outcomes. Keeping those decisions explicit makes both Swift and Dart code easier to understand and test.

items: Keep networking and persistence behind focused interfaces.
Model loading, success, empty, and failure states intentionally.
Let views render state instead of deciding business rules.
Write tests around behavior that is costly to verify manually.

content.text: Architecture is useful when it lowers the cost of change. A small feature does not need layers for their own sake, but it does benefit from names and boundaries that reveal where new behavior belongs.
The best structure is not the one with the most patterns; it is the one that makes the next product decision straightforward to implement.

Small pull requests, targeted tests, and frequent product reviews expose incorrect assumptions early. This feedback loop matters as much as the code structure, because maintainability is also a team habit.
